newsitem.title: USA: Dole hits Clinton on ethics in debate opener.
newsitem.headline: Dole hits Clinton on ethics in debate opener.

text.p: Republican Bob Dole accused President Bill Clinton of presiding over "ethical scandals in the White House" on Wednesday at the start of a final campaign debate that offered Dole a last chance to slow Clinton's bandwagon.

Dole, expected to go on the attack against Clinton, did just that right away by turning a question on what he would do to rekindle faith in government into a jab at Clinton, saying: "No doubt about it that many Americans have lost their faith in government. They see ethical scandals in the White House today."

Dole made a glancing reference to Clinton White House aides improperly collecting FBI files on Republicans, implying Clinton had broken a 1992 campaign pledge to run a clean government. He added: "When I'm president of the United States I will keep my word, my word is my bond."

The Democratic president seemed unfazed by Dole's quick strike, ignoring the specifics in his rebuttal but saying in reply to the original question that he had "done everything I could at every moment of division in this country ... to bring people together."

He took a return shot at Dole with a reference to the highly unpopular move by the Republican Congress to shut down the federal government during a 1995 budget fight. He said the two parties should be working together "instead of shutting down the government in a partisan fight over the budget.

Clinton later accused the Republicans of proposing cuts in the Medicare public health insurance program. That prompted Dole to reply, "There you go again, talking about a Medicare cut." Dole denied the charge, using the opening to recycle a famous presidential debate one-liner -- "there you go again" used with success by Ronald Reagan in his 1980 debate with Jimmy Carter.
